headline: Single-cell multiomics and deep learning map enhancer-gene regulatory programs across…
label: Enhancer Chromatin Regulatory Modeling
summary: Single-cell multiome, QTL and sequence-based deep learning models now resolve enhancer targeting and chromatin accessibility at population scale.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of enhancer-mediated gene regulation from chromatin accessibility, histone marks and DNA sequence, increasingly using single-cell multiomic data. SPARK learns enhancer gene regulatory networks as Bayesian DAGs from single-cell multiome data with prior knowledge, and a graph neural network links caQTL peaks to genes in 3.5M PBMCs from 1,042 donors. Sequence-based models are represented by Scooby-2, which fine-tunes AlphaGenome with a cell-specific decoder for single-cell track prediction, UniLoopNet for multi-type chromatin interactions, and a CNN enhancer predictor applied to Heliconius butterflies. Experimental work includes an SPIE-seq insertion screen across 724 clonal lines testing the regulation-by-partition model. What is new is the joint use of population-scale genetic variation, single-cell resolution and sequence models to map regulatory effects onto specific cell types. The items are heterogeneous and do not establish comparative performance among methods.
